summary.headline: Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 42% YoY to ₹23,900 crore, but EBITDA margin fell 90 bps to 11.7% as a 590 bps commodity headwind was absorbed.
summary.overview: Wholesales grew 42% YoY to 135,100 units, with every segment in double digits and international business up 177% on the Indonesia order. Standalone EBITDA was about ₹2,800 crore (up 31%) and EBIT margin was 9.7%, down 50 bps YoY, as commodity inflation was largely offset by operating leverage, cost efficiency and realisation gains. Free cash flow reached ₹4,600 crore, helped by a ₹2,679 crore working capital release that management said is partly timing-related. Management expects Q3 YoY growth to taper to high single or early double digits, and commodity inflation of a further 150-200 bps in Q3.

segments.name: HCV
segments.commentary: Q2 wholesales up 41% YoY; H1 up 32%. H1 VAHAN market share 55.7%, up 50 bps over FY26.

segments.name: ILMCV
segments.commentary: Q2 wholesales up 24% YoY; H1 up 20%. H1 VAHAN market share 36.3%, partly helped by competitors' supply constraints.

segments.name: SCV and pickup
segments.commentary: Q2 wholesales up 27% YoY; H1 up 30%. H1 market share 27.6%, up 130 bps over FY26. EV salience about 12% in Q2.

segments.name: CV Passenger
segments.commentary: Q2 wholesales up 31% YoY; H1 up 26%. H1 market share 41.1%, up 500 bps over FY26.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Q2 volumes up 177% YoY (about 2.6x), driven by Indonesia deliveries of 4,500-5,000 per month against a ~70,000-unit order. H1 up 114%.

segments.name: EV
segments.commentary: Overall EV volumes up 143% YoY in Q2; SCV EV retails above 4,400 units, 2.9x YoY, constrained by imported aggregate supply.

guidance_outlook: Q3 FY27 demand: management expects high single-digit to early double-digit YoY growth for the overall market, with ILMCV and LCV at double digits, CV passenger at double digits, and HCV and SCV in higher single digits. Q3 FY26 base was up 21.5%.
Commodity inflation: further increase of around 150-200 bps in Q3 FY27, led by steel and rubber. YoY commodity impact is about 540 bps; QoQ (Q1 to Q2) was 200 bps.
Pricing: four actions in FY27 (about 1% in January, 2% in April, 2.5% in July, and 1-2% from 1 October depending on segment). Management said pricing does not fully cover commodity increases.
Working capital: management said part of Q2 working capital release is timing-related and will partly reverse. It expects Q3 and Q4 FCF to remain positive, with Q4 seasonally strong.

IVECO: open offer acceptance period runs to 26 October 2026, offer price raised to EUR14.40 (best and final). About 35% of shares tendered as of 22 October. Settlement expected 30 October 2026, subject to conditions. IVECO consolidation begins next quarter (Q3).
EV salience in SCV pickups expected to rise above Q2's ~12% in Q3 and Q4, with management seeing a potential of up to 20%. Driver is Delhi-NCR EV-only registration rule from 1 January.
Tax is now a recurring cash item and will scale with profit. Q2 tax paid was ₹762 crore vs ₹337 crore a year ago.
capex_capacity: Q2 capex was ₹483 crore, in line with last year and plan. Q2 investment spend was ₹597 crore vs ₹686 crore a year ago; H1 investment ₹1,112 crore. R&D was ₹339 crore in Q2 (₹209 crore capitalised, ₹130 crore expensed), about 2.5% of revenue within the 2-4% guided range.

Capacity constraints are in the supply chain (castings, machining, sheet metal stamping, proprietary items and imported EV aggregates, especially battery cells). Some demand was lost in ILMCV and electric SCV.
Targeted in-house debottlenecking was done in Q2 and will continue through Q3 and partly in Q4, in anticipation of Q4 demand. No new large capacity addition was announced.
Smart City e-bus operations maintain more than 95% fleet uptime and have covered over 64 crore green km since inception.
demand_pricing: Industry CV offtake grew 28.4% YoY in Q2 versus Tata Motors' 30.5%. Fleet utilisation improved gradually through Q2 and freight rates strengthened, though transporter profitability was hit early in the quarter by the diesel price increase.

Domestic ASPs rose QoQ and YoY, but total ASP was flat because of the higher mix of light and small commercial vehicles in the Indonesia export order. International business remains margin accretive, though Indonesia is ASP-dilutive.
Commodity headwind of 590 bps in Q2 EBIT margin walk; steel at a 52-week high, up about 40% YoY. Management has requested a review of the steel safeguard duty through SIAM and other channels.
Interest rates: a 25 bps hike has been taken. Management flagged diesel prices and interest rates as key demand monitorables.
No credit stress seen among transport financiers the company has spoken to. Management says they are in a good place, though not all financiers were engaged.
Non-cyclical business is about 20% of revenue, a stated focus area to offset cyclicality.

qa_highlights.question: How much more commodity pressure is expected next quarter, and what price hikes have been taken?
qa_highlights.answer: Commodity impact is about 540 bps YoY and 200 bps QoQ. Another 150-200 bps is expected in Q3. Four pricing actions were taken in FY27, with a further 1-2% from 1 October; this does not fully cover the commodity increase.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Indonesia delivery plan for FY27-FY28, and is there repeat business beyond?
qa_highlights.answer: The ~70,000-unit order will be delivered over FY27 and FY28, currently at 4,500-5,000 units per month. Management is building retail finance, distribution and service in Indonesia and plans to use the opening to sell other segments.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any hurdle to reaching the 80% IVECO threshold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the transaction is progressing in line with expectations. It cited the IVECO EGM approval and the best-and-final EUR14.40 offer, and expects tendering to be concentrated in the final 24-48 hours.

qa_highlights.question: Is there concern on transporter sentiment given lower YoY utilisation in HCV, ICV cargo and SCV?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation started weaker in Q2 but improved consistently through the quarter, which gave management enough confidence that it is in a good place.

qa_highlights.question: Are export margins accretive and why were ASPs flat?
qa_highlights.answer: International is margin accretive, but Indonesia is LCV-and-below and so ASP-dilutive. Domestic ASPs rose QoQ and YoY; the flat total ASP reflects the mix shift to smaller vehicles in the Indonesia order.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q2 working capital release reverses in H2, and what is normalised FY27 FCF?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a number. It said Q1 and Q2 were cash positive, and expects Q3 and Q4 to stay positive, with Q4 seasonally strong.

risks_watch: Commodity inflation: management expects a further 150-200 bps QoQ in Q3 FY27 (steel and rubber), after about 540 bps YoY; four price actions in FY27 do not fully cover it, with a further 1-2% from 1 October.

Demand taper: Q3 FY27 growth guided to high single-digit to early double-digit YoY vs a 21.5% base in Q3 FY26; HCV and SCV seen in higher single digits; diesel prices and a 25 bps rate hike flagged as monitorables.
Working capital: about ₹2,679 crore release in Q2 is partly timing-related and will partially reverse as payables normalise; no quantum given for the reversal.
Supply constraints: castings, machining, sheet metal stamping, proprietary items and imported EV battery cells; management admits lost demand in ILMCV and electric SCV.
IVECO: open offer closes 26 October 2026, settlement expected 30 October 2026 subject to conditions; about 35% tendered as of 22 October; consolidation from Q3.

Indonesia order (~70,000 units, 4,500-5,000 per month) is ASP-dilutive; no clarity given on repeat orders beyond FY28. EV salience in SCV pickups targeted at up to 20% in Q4 on the Delhi-NCR EV-only rule from 1 January; ADAS cost impact not yet quantified.
key_quotes: It certainly doesn't cover the commodity increases that we have seen.
So, I do see a potential of the EV salience reaching easily up to 20%.
I would want to mention here that part of this working capital release is timing -related and will partially reverse as payables normalize as we move forward.
We therefore remain confident of a successful completion of the open offer.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volumes, market share and IVECO completion, but cautious on margins, pricing and demand, with management repeatedly stressing that price hikes do not fully cover commodity inflation. Evasive on specifics: no quantum for the working capital reversal, no FY28 margin target, no ADAS cost estimate and no EV cost outlook, with several questions deferred offline.

adds.what: Targeted in-house debottlenecking (castings, machining, sheet metal stamping) through Q3 and partly Q4; no new large capacity addition announced

growth.why: Management guides Q3 CV industry growth to high single to early double digits, with Q3 YoY growth tapering from Q2's 42% and commodity headwinds of 150-200 bps more; growth is backed partly by the ~70,000-unit Indonesia order (4,500-5,000/month), pricing actions and share gains, while capacity additions are limited to in-house debottlenecking in Q3-Q4.
